title: Traitor to His Class: The Privileged Life and Radical Presidency of Franklin Delano Roosevelt
author: H. W. Brands
target_audience: Students and scholars of presidential leadership
General audience seeking insight into FDR’s impact
core_themes: Transformation of American society through the New Deal
FDR’s political evolution and leadership style
Navigating crisis: The Great Depression and World War II
Role of personality and background in shaping public policy
primary_purpose: To chronicle the complex life and presidency of Franklin D. Roosevelt, exploring how a man born to privilege became a champion of the common citizen and fundamentally changed the role of government in American society.

structure_format.organization: Organized into three main parts: early life and upbringing, ascent in politics, and presidency (including the New Deal and World War II years)
features: In-depth portraits of major contemporaries and rivals
A balance of personal anecdote and political narrative

key_concepts_lessons: Personal background can profoundly influence political values and decision-making.
Transformational leadership often involves betraying the very class or group from which one originates.
Crisis demands both bold action and empathetic reassurance—a combination FDR mastered.
Presidential power expands in response to public expectation and extraordinary historical circumstances.
Effective political communication (‘Fireside Chats’) builds public confidence and unity.
notable_features: Balanced portrayal that acknowledges both FDR’s achievements and his flaws
Exploration of FDR's complicated marriage and private life
Insight into FDR's use of media and communication
Contextualization within broader economic and global trends
cultural_historical_context: Written during a period of renewed interest in presidential power and social reforms, the book connects FDR's legacy to ongoing debates about government responsibility and progressive leadership, particularly relevant in late 2000s America (the Great Recession era).
reception_impact: Critically acclaimed for its thorough research and narrative skill
Praised for humanizing a monumental historical figure while unpacking the intricacies of his presidency
Recognized as a comprehensive resource on FDR, cited in academic and popular contexts
Shortlisted for several major awards, and helped cement H.W. Brands’ status as a leading biographer
comparable_titles: Franklin D. Roosevelt: A Rendezvous with Destiny by Frank Freidel
No Ordinary Time: Franklin & Eleanor Roosevelt: The Home Front in World War II by Doris Kearns Goodwin
The Defining Moment: FDR's Hundred Days and the Triumph of Hope by Jonathan Alter
